title: Redefining What Quality Care Means with Kultar Garcha, MD, Chief Medical Officer of the UK & EMEA
summary: Hims & Hers named Kultar Garcha, MD, as Chief Medical Officer of the UK and EMEA. Hear from Dr. Garcha on his path into medicine, why he joined Hims & Hers, and what's ahead for clinical care across the region.
body_markdown:
We’re excited to introduce Kultar Garcha, MD, as Chief Medical Officer of Hims & Hers UK and EMEA. Dr. Garcha brings nearly two decades of experience across public and private UK and international health systems, and almost 15 years as a practicing GP. He also sits on NICE's Quality Standards Advisory Committee, helping set the standards that guide care improvement across England.


Now he's bringing that experience to Hims & Hers, where he's leading medical strategy across the UK and EMEA. We sat down with him to talk about his path into medicine, the gap in care he's spent his career chasing, and what he's building next.


##### **What first drew you to practicing medicine?**


I always wanted to be a doctor. My dad's a GP, so I grew up watching him work and wanted to follow in his footsteps. But I didn't plan on general practice. On my first day as a junior doctor, I realized hospital medicine wasn't for me. I'm biased, but I've come to think general practice is the best specialty in medicine, and it's one of the most rewarding. My favorite consultations still aren't really about practicing medicine at all — they're the ones where someone just needed to be heard, and they leave feeling like a different person.


##### After nearly 20 years in the NHS, what's the gap you keep running into?


Our health systems are built for sick care, even the way we diagnose reflects that. Perimenopause is a good example. The symptoms start well before there's a clean threshold to diagnose against, and a standard ten-minute appointment isn't built for a conversation that complicated. Perinatal mental health runs into the same wall. Both take time to properly unpack, and the system isn’t set up to give people that time. That isn’t good enough.


I've watched the NHS make real progress here, with the NHS App and a plan to move care from analogue to digital, but the system is still funded to treat, not to keep people well. Closing that gap is what pulled me toward digital health in the first place.


##### **What drew you to Hims & Hers?**


The way the platform meets people where they are, instead of asking them to find their way into a system built around institutions. It's doctor-led, which matters to me; I saw that commitment firsthand meeting with the team. And the whole model is built around staying well, which is the piece most of the healthcare system is missing.


##### **You've said the standard of care someone gets shouldn't depend on where they live or how well they can navigate the system. What does that look like in practice?**


A lot of what shapes someone's health happens outside a doctor's office entirely. The differences in life expectancy within the same country, even the same city, show how far there is to go. In practice, it means starting from someone's circumstances, not a script, and rethinking what quality, in the clinical sense, actually measures. I’m a big believer in patient-reported outcomes: does this care actually improve someone’s day-to-day life? To me, that is just as important as any clinical marker. It means offering the same standard of care no matter how someone comes to us, and checking whether it's working means actually asking people how they feel, which a chart alone can't tell you.


##### **What are you hoping to build in this role?**


My focus is clinical quality, patient safety, and prescribing standards across the UK and EMEA – safe, high-quality care to as many people as possible, especially the people who don't always access care, whether they don't know how or feel there's a stigma in asking.


If there's one thing I'd tell someone who's never used a platform like ours: don't wait until something's wrong to look after your health. The earlier we can help, the better, and this is built to last beyond a single visit.
